name: Simone Web: Super Admin – Security & Performance
author: Simone Manfredini

sections.description:
When you build or manage a site for a client, the client usually needs an administrator account, but you don’t want them to install plugins, switch themes or edit files by mistake. Simone Web: Super Admin – Security & Performance adds a “Super Admin” level above the administrators of a single site: Super Admins keep every capability, the other administrators lose only what you decide.

The user who activates the plugin becomes the main Super Admin and can grant the same access to other administrators. The settings page is visible to Super Admins only.

This is not the Super Admin role of WordPress multisite: it works on a single site and only affects the plugin’s own permissions.

Super Admin

  • Pick which administrators are Super Admins.
  • The main Super Admin can’t be removed from the interface, and nobody can remove their own access.

Restrictions for the other administrators

  • Disable update management, theme management, plugin management and the theme/plugin file editor.
  • Restrict advanced block editor features (block locking, code editor, Font Library) to Super Admins.
  • Show the ACF admin interface to Super Admins only.
  • Restrictions are applied at runtime: nothing is written to the users’ capabilities, and deactivating the plugin restores them immediately.

Security

  • Disable XML-RPC and the X-Pingback header.
  • Clean the head: WordPress version, RSD, WLW, shortlink, feed, REST API and oEmbed links.
  • Disable emoji scripts and styles.
  • Generic login error message.
  • Block user enumeration (REST API users endpoint, ?author=N URLs, users sitemap, author in oEmbed).
  • Security headers: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy.
  • Block access to hidden files and wp-config.php, hide PHP errors and disable directory listing via .htaccess (Apache).
  • Optional: redirect HTTP to HTTPS, disable automatic updates, disable application passwords.

Performance

  • Remove jQuery Migrate and move jQuery to the footer.
  • Deflate compression and browser caching rules (Apache).
  • Limit post revisions and remove unused image sizes (medium_large, 1536×1536, 2048×2048).
  • Reduce or disable the Heartbeat API on the frontend.
  • Disable remote block patterns from the WordPress.org Pattern Directory.

Tools

  • Disable comments (WooCommerce product reviews keep working).
  • Keep subscribers out of the dashboard and hide their admin bar.
  • Hide the frontend admin bar for everyone, to check the layout as visitors see it.
  • Block editor defaults: not fullscreen, List View open, SEO boxes (Yoast SEO, Rank Math) at the bottom.

Every option can be turned on or off individually. The options that are active by default only remove things most sites don’t need, and each one can be turned off.

sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard go to Plugins → Add New Plugin, search for “Simone Web Super Admin” and click Install Now, or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin. The user who activates it becomes the main Super Admin and is taken to the settings page.
  3. Configure the plugin under Settings → Simone Web: Super Admin (visible to Super Admins only).
sections.faq:
Who becomes Super Admin?

The user who activates the plugin becomes the main Super Admin. From the Super Admin tab they can give the same access to other administrators. Super Admins see the settings page and are never affected by the restrictions.

Is this the same as the WordPress multisite Super Admin?

No. It is a role added by this plugin on a single site, on top of the normal Administrator role. It doesn’t change the multisite network roles.

I activated the plugin but I can’t see the settings page

Only Super Admins see it. If the plugin was activated without a logged-in user (for example with WP-CLI), nobody became Super Admin: deactivate and reactivate the plugin from the Plugins screen while logged in as the administrator who should manage it.

What happens to the other administrators?

Nothing, until you enable a restriction in the Security tab. Then they lose only the capabilities you chose (updates, themes, plugins, file editor) and keep everything else.

Does the plugin slow down my site?

No. Options are read from memory and restrictions are calculated when WordPress checks a capability, without extra database queries. The performance options remove scripts, requests and image sizes that most sites don’t need.

How do I enable HTTPS redirection?

Enable the “Redirect HTTPS” option in the Security tab to automatically redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS.

Can I keep XML-RPC enabled?

Yes. XML-RPC is disabled by default; untick “Disable XML-RPC” in the Security tab if you need it (e.g. for the WordPress mobile app or Jetpack).

Can I disable theme and plugin editing for administrators?

Yes, you can disable file editing for non-super admin users by enabling the “Disable File Edit” option in the settings.

Can I turn off automatic updates?

Yes. Enable “Disable Automatic Updates” in the Security tab to stop background updates of WordPress core, plugins, themes and translations. It is off by default; when enabled, updates (including security releases) must be installed manually.

Should I disable application passwords?

Only if nothing connects to your site with one. “Disable Application Passwords” in the Security tab is off by default: when enabled, apps and services that authenticate to the REST API with an application password (AI assistants, mobile apps, automation tools) stop working.

Will disabling comments affect WooCommerce reviews?

No. Product reviews keep working and the Comments screen stays available to moderate them.

Does “Block Sensitive Files” block the /.well-known/ folder?

No. Hidden files such as .env, .git and .htpasswd are blocked, but /.well-known/ stays reachable because SSL certificate validation, OAuth discovery and app links need it.

Why are the .htaccess rules not applied?

They need Apache and a permalink structure other than “Plain”. On Nginx, add the equivalent rules to the server configuration. The plugin shows a notice in these cases. After an update the rules are rewritten automatically the first time an administrator opens the dashboard.

My site shows a 500 error after activating the plugin

Some hosts don’t allow the Options directive in .htaccess. Remove the “Options -Indexes” line from .htaccess, then untick “Disable Directory Listing” in the Security tab. Every .htaccess rule written by the plugin can be turned off from the Security and Performance tabs.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

On deactivation the plugin’s rules are removed from .htaccess and the restrictions stop immediately. On deletion all plugin options are removed, together with the Super Admin capabilities the plugin stored on users.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: Tools tab with options to disable comments (WooCommerce reviews excluded), restrict subscribers, hide the frontend admin bar for everyone and adjust block editor defaults.
  • New: Security options to disable automatic updates, block user enumeration, send security headers, disable application passwords, restrict advanced editor features, hide PHP errors and disable directory listing.
  • New: Performance options for revisions limit, unused image sizes, Heartbeat and remote block patterns.
  • New: after activation the settings page opens automatically.
  • New: Settings link in the Plugins screen.
  • New: .htaccess rules are rewritten automatically after a plugin update, so fixes and new rules apply without saving the permalinks.
  • Changed: the General tab is now called Super Admin; Security options reordered and shorter labels.
  • Fixed: .htaccess rules compatible with Apache 2.4 and with servers without mod_setenvif or mod_headers.
  • Fixed: Block Sensitive Files no longer blocks /.well-known/ URLs (OAuth discovery, SSL validation, app links); other hidden files stay blocked.
  • Fixed: settings tab names are now translatable.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
